headline: Approved revisions to CDBG grant application questions on priority impact, community need, financial need, and leveraged funding.
summary: The task force reviewed proposed CDBG application questions to align with scoring categories and HUD metrics, and discussed diversity, financial need, and the Neighborly application portal. Members approved changes to several application sections covering priority impact, community need, diversity and inclusiveness, sustainability, location, financial need, and leveraged funding categories.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes, 4 yays to 3 abstentions.
Approved instructions requiring applicants to select the one goal that best aligns with their project.
Approved adding a prompt asking applicants to identify their target audience and explain community involvement in design and leadership.
Voted to consolidate two redundant diversity and inclusiveness questions into one 10-point question, subject to Corporation Council review.
Agreed to keep prompts asking for the percentage of LMI individuals served and how income levels are verified.
Approved updating sustainability language to ask how the project will maintain or increase service delivery.
Voted to split the construction location prompt into identifying census tract and describing LMI area impact.
Approved asking construction applicants how the project meets or exceeds Portland's development standards and building codes.
Voted to merge two financial need questions into one, requiring applicants to justify their financial gap.
Approved categorizing leveraged funding status into three options: Applied, Pending/Pledged, or Committed.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to approve the previous meeting minutes passed (4 yays, 3 abstentions).
Approved instructions requiring applicants to select the one goal that best aligns with their project.
Approved adding a prompt asking applicants to identify their target audience and explain how they involve that community in program design and leadership.
Voted to consolidate two redundant questions into one 10-point question focusing on how the project addresses barriers and responds to community needs, subject to Corporation Council review.
Agreed to maintain prompts asking for the percentage of LMI individuals served and a description of how those income levels (or presumed benefit status) are verified.
Approved updating language to ask how the project will "maintain or increase service delivery" and aid sustainability beyond the grant period.
Voted to split the prompt to ask applicants to identify their census tract on the eligible map, and then describe how the project positively impacts the LMI area.
Approved asking how the project meets or exceeds Portland's development standards and building codes, deferring questions about past construction experience to the "Capacity to Deliver" section.
Voted to merge two questions into one, explicitly stating CDBG cannot replace existing funds, and asking applicants to justify their financial gap.
Approved categorizing the status of other funding sources into three distinct options: Applied, Pending/Pledged, or Committed.
